title: Calisthenics — Beginner Basics
subtitle: Building the foundational push/pull/core patterns
coaching_note: Calisthenics is a skill practice as much as a strength one — clean reps in a smaller range beat sloppy reps in a bigger one. Every exercise here has a regression built into the cue; use it without ego if the full version breaks down.

exercises.name: Wrist Circles & Stretches
exercises.form_cue: Full range both directions, spend extra time on any stiff spot.
exercises.why: Your wrists take load in every plank and push position — warm them up first, always.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.form_cue: Slow and deliberate, full spinal flexion and extension.
exercises.why: Wakes the spine up and previews the hollow body shape you'll hold later.

exercises.name: Incline Push-up
exercises.form_cue: Hands on a stable elevated surface, straight body line, chest touches the surface each rep.
exercises.why: The incline reduces load compared to a floor push-up so you build clean full-range reps — that's what earns you the harder version.

exercises.name: Wall Handstand Hold
exercises.form_cue: Face away from the wall, walk your feet up until your hands and shoulders are stacked. Push the floor away, squeeze your core.
exercises.why: Introduces you to inverted body positions early — the entry point for every handstand skill later on.

exercises.name: Doorframe Row (towel or sturdy edge)
exercises.form_cue: Lean back holding a sturdy anchor, pull your chest toward your hands, squeeze the shoulder blades together.
exercises.why: Bodyweight pulling strength almost never gets trained without a bar — this is your entry into it.

exercises.name: Dead Hang (if a bar is available)
exercises.form_cue: Full grip, relaxed shoulders, let your body hang straight.
exercises.why: Grip and shoulder capsule prep for every pull-up progression to come — start banking hang time now.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.form_cue: Lower back pressed flat on the floor, arms overhead, legs straight and low. If your back arches, bring your legs higher.
exercises.why: The hollow body shape underlies almost every calisthenics skill — start building the position and the endurance now.

exercises.name: Chest Opener Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Arms behind your back, clasp your hands, squeeze your shoulder blades, open your chest toward the ceiling.
exercises.why: Counters the pushing and pulling work — keeps posture from rounding forward as you build strength.

progression_notes: Once 3x10 incline push-ups feel controlled, lower the incline. Once 20s hollow body holds feel solid, extend to 25-30s before adding leg lowers.
